```sql
WITH ol_agg AS (
    SELECT ol.order_id,
           ol.variant_id,
           sum(ol.quantity)         AS qty,
           sum(ol.line_total_cents) AS rev
      FROM order_lines ol
     WHERE ol.order_id IN (
             SELECT o.id
               FROM orders o
              WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
                AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
                AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
                AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
           )
     GROUP BY ol.order_id, ol.variant_id
),
per_product AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           count(DISTINCT a.order_id) AS order_count,
           sum(a.qty)::bigint         AS quantity,
           sum(a.rev)                 AS revenue_cents,
           count(DISTINCT pv.id)      AS variant_count
      FROM ol_agg a
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = a.variant_id::uuid
     GROUP BY pv.product_id
     ORDER BY quantity DESC, revenue_cents DESC
     LIMIT %(limit)s
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       pp.order_count,
       pp.quantity,
       pp.revenue_cents,
       pp.variant_count
  FROM per_product pp
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pp.product_id
 ORDER BY pp.quantity DESC, pp.revenue_cents DESC
```

De orderregels worden eerst per (order, variant) voorgeaggregeerd. Daardoor zijn er veel minder lookups in `product_variants` nodig en blijven `count(DISTINCT ...)` en de sommen exact gelijk; `quantity` wordt teruggecast naar `bigint` zodat het type overeenkomt. De brede `products`-rijen (met onder andere `thumbnail` en `description`) worden pas na de LIMIT opgehaald. Dat kan veilig, omdat `pv.product_id` een NOT NULL foreign key is en de join dus 1-op-1 is.
